nyc_found: "Approximately 7,000 miles of water mains, tunnels and aqueducts bring water to homes and businesses throughout the five boroughs" (nyc.gov DEP hydrant-use release)
match_found: "about 7,341 miles of mainlines and trunk lines and approximately 300 miles of water conveyance system along the Los Angeles Aqueduct" (LADWP 2024-25 Water Infrastructure Plan, p.2); the 7,341 figure breaks down as 6,794 miles of mainline pipe plus 547 miles of trunk line pipe, per pages 3-4
finding: The numbers and the 7,341/7,000 = 1.049 ratio check out, but the two sides measure different things: NYC's 7,000-mile figure explicitly bundles water mains with tunnels and upstate aqueducts, while LA's 7,341-mile figure is local mainlines and trunk lines only and specifically excludes its own 300-mile Los Angeles Aqueduct system. Comparing NYC's aqueduct-inclusive total to LA's aqueduct-exclusive total overstates how close the two distribution systems actually are.
